subject.title: feat: audit PR review convergence at exact head

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this repository-local convergence audit as a merge-decision input, including the maintenance commitment to resolve required checks from GitHub branch protection and ruleset policy?
rationale: The mechanical defect is clear, but choosing a durable policy source and deciding whether this new audit should become part of the repository’s merge workflow are product and automation-ownership decisions.

options.title: Adopt with policy-backed required checks
options.body: Keep the pilot, add authoritative target-branch required-check resolution with UNKNOWN on ambiguity, and require live proof before workflow adoption.

options.title: Keep it as an experimental diagnostic
options.body: Retain a clearly non-authoritative report-only tool and avoid using its READY result for merge decisions until policy ownership is established.

options.title: Decline the new audit surface
options.body: Close the direction and continue relying on the existing review and proof-policy workflow rather than adding a parallel convergence system.

recommendation.title: Adopt with policy-backed required checks
recommendation.body: Keep the pilot, add authoritative target-branch required-check resolution with UNKNOWN on ambiguity, and require live proof before workflow adoption.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposed script directly composes the existing ClawSweeper proof-policy integration and the prior automation reviews identified the unresolved contract.
